subtitle: When Stone Remembered What Voices Forgot

panels.shot: low-angle close-up of a carved stone pillar coiled with a serpent, Ahom letters cut into its face, with a distant royal court blurred behind
panels.action: Suhungmung and his Ahom scribes stand behind a looming stone pillar wrapped in a carved serpent, the faint lines of Ahom script glinting in the soft Assam light, palace roofs just visible beyond.

dialogue.text: In Suhungmung’s Assam, a serpent pillar in Ahom script turns from stone to witness, where court memory begins to harden into record and legend meets the first firm cuts of history.

i18n.hi: सुहंगमूंग के असम में, अहोम-लिपि वाला नाग‑स्तंभ पत्थर से गवाह बन जाता है, जहाँ दरबार की याद रिकॉर्ड बनती है और कथाएँ इतिहास की पहली कतरनों से टकराती हैं।

panels.shot: wide aerial shot over the Brahmaputra valley, mist over river and forested hills, tiny clearings of villages and embankments below
panels.action: The misty Brahmaputra winds across dense green forests and scattered clearings of early sixteenth-century Upper Assam, smoke from village hearths rising into the pale dawn.

dialogue.text: Long before presses and printed laws, the Brahmaputra valley held kingdoms whose memory lived in voices, drums and palm leaves more than in stone.

i18n.hi: छापाखाने और मुद्रित कानूनों से बहुत पहले, ब्रह्मपुत्र घाटी के राज बसते थे ढोल, आवाज़ों और ताड़पत्रों की याद में, पत्थर से भी ज़्यादा।

panels.shot: intimate interior mid-shot of a chronicler reading from a palm-leaf manuscript by lamplight, shadows large on the wall
panels.action: An Ahom court chronicler sits cross-legged in a dim hall, lamp beside him, tracing his finger along a palm leaf as nobles listen in a half-circle, their faces lit by flickering flame.

dialogue.text: Later called Buranjis, these court chronicles stitched rulers and battles into careful prose, but much of early time was written down only after the dust had settled.

i18n.hi: जिन्हें बाद में बुरांजी कहा गया, वे दरबारी इतिहास राजाओं और युद्धों को नपी‑तुली गद्य में पिरोते हैं, पर शुरुआती ज़माने का बहुत सा लेखा बाद में, धूल थमने के बाद ही लिखा गया।

panels.shot: slow push-in on a painted scene of Sukaphaa’s migration, then a ghostly overlay of a question mark over the dates and route
panels.action: A mural-like scene shows a Tai-Ahom group crossing a river with their animals, the image fading at the edges into mist as the path and date blur into uncertainty.

dialogue.text: Tradition speaks of Sukaphaa crossing into Assam, some say in 1228, yet careful scholars like Christian Daniels remind us that even this date rests on later memory, not firm inscription.

i18n.hi: परंपरा सुकाफ़ा के असम में घुसने की बात करती है, कुछ इसे 1228 मानते हैं, पर क्रिश्चियन डेनियल्स जैसे विद्वान याद दिलाते हैं कि यह तारीख भी बाद की स्मृति पर टिकी है, किसी पक्की लिखत पर नहीं।

panels.shot: side view of a scholar in a modern archive turning pages of different Buranji manuscripts laid out together
panels.action: A modern historian in a quiet archive bends over a table strewn with Buranji manuscripts, each in neat Ahom and Assamese scripts, noting differences with a reed pen.

dialogue.text: Buranjis preserve remarkable detail, but early entries were often compiled later, revised and recopied. To test them, historians turn to mute witnesses: coins, bricks, and rare stones.

i18n.hi: बुरांजी अद्भुत बारीकियाँ बचाए रखते हैं, पर शुरुआती हिस्से अक्सर बाद में जोड़े, सुधारे और फिर नकल किए गए। इन्हें परखने को इतिहासकार गूँगे गवाह ढूँढते हैं – सिक्के, ईंटें और विरली शिलाएँ।

panels.shot: medium shot of Suhungmung in council with scribes and priests in a timber-pillared hall, maps and objects laid before them
panels.action: King Suhungmung sits on a low throne in a timber hall, Ahom scribes with palm leaves and priests with ritual objects standing before him as they discuss matters of rule.

dialogue.text: By the early sixteenth century, under Suhungmung, the Ahom kingdom in Upper Assam was expanding and hardening, its rituals more formal, its court more crowded, its need for enduring memory greater.

i18n.hi: सोलहवीं सदी की शुरुआत तक, सुहंगमूंग के समय ऊपरी असम का अहोम राज फैल रहा था, सख़्त हो रहा था; अनुष्ठान ज़्यादा औपचारिक, दरबार भरा‑भरा, और टिकाऊ याद की भूख गहरी।

panels.shot: close-up on the hands of an Ahom scribe practicing characters on a palm leaf, Suhungmung’s figure blurred in the background
panels.action: An Ahom scribe’s steady hands etch curving characters onto a palm leaf with a stylus, while Suhungmung’s form looms indistinct behind him, watching.

dialogue.text: The Ahom script, with its flowing lines, likely evolved from earlier Tai writing, yet it steps into clear view only now, on palm leaf and, for the first time, on stone.

i18n.hi: लहरदार रेखाओं वाली अहोम लिपि शायद पुरानी ताई लिखावट से निकली, पर साफ़ नज़र आती है अब – ताड़पत्रों पर, और पहली बार पत्थर पर।

panels.shot: wide shot of a sacred precinct near Sivasagar, priests showing Suhungmung a spot where a pillar might stand
panels.action: Near a pond and grove outside the royal center, priests gesture toward a cleared patch of earth as Suhungmung and his scribes consider the place, bamboo scaffolding stacked nearby.

dialogue.text: In the royal heartland around what is now Sivasagar, a plan took shape: to fix in stone a sign of royal authority, ritual, and language, where only passing structures stood before.

i18n.hi: आज के शिवसागर के आसपास शाही दिल में एक योजना बनी – जहाँ पहले बस मिटने वाले ढाँचे थे, वहाँ पत्थर में ही राज, अनुष्ठान और भाषा की मुहर बैठानी है।

panels.shot: low-angle shot of a stonecutter carving a serpent winding up a pillar shaft, Suhungmung and a scribe watching from above the frame
panels.action: A stone mason chips a serpent curling around a rising pillar, his chisel paused as he looks up to where Suhungmung and an Ahom scribe confer at the edge of the worksite.

dialogue.text: “Let the nāg coil around our words, so earth and sky know who rules.”

i18n.hi: “नाग हमारे शब्दों को लपेट ले, ताकि धरती‑आसमान जानें, राज किसका है।”

panels.shot: extreme close-up on freshly carved Ahom characters on the pillar, stone dust still clinging in the grooves
panels.action: Tiny curls of stone dust cling to sharply cut Ahom letters on the pillar’s smooth face as the scribe leans in, examining the fresh inscription.

dialogue.text: The Snake Pillar inscription of Suhungmung bears royal words in Ahom script, marking one of the earliest moments when this language of rule steps boldly onto stone.

i18n.hi: सुहंगमूंग के नाग‑स्तंभ पर अहोम लिपि में उकेरे शाही शब्द हैं, यह उन शुरुआती पलों में से एक को चिन्हित करता है जब यह राजभाषा बेख़ौफ़ पत्थर पर उतरती है।

panels.shot: medium shot of Suhungmung touching the carved letters while the scribe recites them softly
panels.action: Suhungmung rests his fingers lightly on the incised lines as the Ahom scribe beside him recites the text with lowered eyes in a hushed tone.

dialogue.text: The inscription anchors royal acts to place and time, tying Suhungmung’s name, rituals and claims to a stone that does not forget when voices are silenced.

i18n.hi: यह लेख शाही कामों को जगह और समय में गाड़ देता है, सुहंगमूंग का नाम, अनुष्ठान और दावे एक ऐसे पत्थर से बाँध देता है जो आवाज़ें चुप होने पर भी नहीं भूलता।

panels.shot: wide ceremonial shot of the completed pillar erected, priests, soldiers and courtiers gathered around in a formal rite
panels.action: The fully raised serpent pillar stands upright as priests pour water at its base, soldiers and courtiers ring it in a wide circle, Suhungmung standing slightly apart in quiet pride.

dialogue.text: Set up in the sacred ground of the royal center, the Snake Pillar spoke not in song but in script, a public, enduring sign that the Ahom state now imprinted itself into the land.

i18n.hi: राजधानी की पवित्र ज़मीन में खड़ा यह नाग‑स्तंभ गीत नहीं, लिपि में बोलता था – एक खुला, टिकाऊ निशान कि अब अहोम राज खुद को ज़मीन पर उकेल रहा है।

panels.shot: time-lapse style wide shot of the pillar as seasons change around it, people of different generations passing by
panels.action: The stone pillar remains motionless as monsoon rain, winter mist and bright summer sun sweep around it, villagers, soldiers and officials from different generations pausing by its base.

dialogue.text: As years rolled by, the pillar outlived courtiers and commanders, its serpent and letters weathering yet legible, a point where memory and landscape fused.

i18n.hi: साल गुजरते गए, स्तंभ ने दरबारियों और सेनापतियों को पीछे छोड़ दिया; उसका नाग और अक्षर घिसे, पर पढ़ने लायक रहे – एक बिंदु जहाँ स्मृति और धरती घुल गईं।

panels.shot: modern-era medium shot of Edward Gait sketching or copying the inscription on site, with local guides nearby
panels.action: A European scholar, Edward Gait, stands by the worn pillar in a later century, notebook open as he carefully sketches the inscription, a local guide pointing to faint lines.

dialogue.text: Centuries later, Edward Gait and others walked this ground, copying the faded Ahom letters to test the old Buranjis against what the stone still remembered.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद एडवर्ड गेट और दूसरे यहाँ चले, फींकी पड़ चुकी अहोम लिखावट उतारते हुए, ताकि पुरानी बुरांजी को उस पत्थर से परखें जो अभी भी याद रखे बैठा था।

panels.shot: interior shot of a modern scholar like Christian Daniels comparing a rubbing of the inscription with a Buranji manuscript on a desk
panels.action: A present-day scholar in an office spreads a rubbing of the Snake Pillar inscription beside a printed Buranji text, tracing dates and names between the two with a pencil.

dialogue.text: Scholars like Christian Daniels read these cuts in stone alongside chronicles, finding where they confirm, where they correct, and where they warn us that early dates and tales may be retrospective.

i18n.hi: क्रिश्चियन डेनियल्स जैसे विद्वान इन पत्थर की कतरनों को इतिहास‑ग्रंथों के साथ पढ़ते हैं – कहाँ ये पुष्टि करते हैं, कहाँ सुधारते हैं, और कहाँ चेतावनी देते हैं कि पुराने किस्से और तारीखें पीछे मुड़कर गढ़ी भी हो सकती हैं।

panels.shot: extreme close-up of the weathered Ahom snake-pillar, its ancient angular Tai-Ahom script worn shallow and indistinct, NO legible letters and absolutely NO Devanagari, warm raking light across the carved grooves and the coiled serpent relief
panels.action: the camera lingers on the pillar's eroded carved surface, the marks deliberately weathered and unreadable, emphasizing age and endurance rather than any single word

dialogue.text: This single pillar runs like a peg through time, anchoring Suhungmung’s reign and the visibility of the Ahom script amid shifting tales of earlier kings and migrations.

i18n.hi: यह अकेला स्तंभ समय में धँसे खूंटे जैसा है, सुहंगमूंग के राज को और अहोम लिपि की झलक को पुराने राजाओं और यात्राओं की डोलती कथाओं के बीच जकड़ता हुआ।

panels.shot: reflective wide shot of the pillar today, slightly worn, with distant modern town structures visible beyond trees
panels.action: The weathered snake pillar stands today under open sky, its softened serpent and faint letters framed by trees, with the outlines of a modern town just visible beyond.

dialogue.text: We cannot yet trace every early line of Ahom writing, nor hold 1228 as unshakable, but this stone shows that by Suhungmung’s age, royal memory, ritual and script had begun to trust themselves to rock.

i18n.hi: हम अभी हर शुरुआती अहोम पंक्ति नहीं पकड़ पाए, न ही 1228 को अटल मान सकते हैं, पर यह पत्थर दिखाता है कि सुहंगमूंग के ज़माने तक शाही स्मृति, अनुष्ठान और लिपि ने खुद को चट्टान पर भरोसे से सौंपना शुरू कर दिया था।

panels.shot: final contemplative close-up of a modern hand brushing moss from the carved letters, sunlight catching on the grooves
panels.action: A modern visitor’s hand gently brushes moss from the carved letters on the pillar as a shaft of sunlight catches in the grooves, making the old script shine for a moment.

dialogue.text: In the Snake Pillar’s quiet script, we see how a spoken kingdom learns to steady its past, and how every written line, cut with care, can hold a people’s memory against the erasures of time.

i18n.hi: नाग‑स्तंभ की शांत लिखावट में दिखता है कि बोले‑भाले राज कैसे अपने अतीत को संभालना सीखते हैं, और कैसे हर तराशी गई पंक्ति, संभालकर काटी गई, किसी कौम की याद को समय की मिटावट से बचाकर रख सकती है।

title_i18n.en: The Snake Pillar Speaks in Ahom Script
title_i18n.hi: अहोम लिपि में बोलता नाग स्तंभ

subtitle_i18n.en: When Stone Remembered What Voices Forgot
subtitle_i18n.hi: जब पत्थर ने याद किया, जो आवाज़ें भूल गईं
